subject.title: Session lane starvation: followup drain monopolizes session lane, blocks inbound dispatch for 20-30min

question: Should OpenClaw make foreground user/control traffic preempt, defer, or cap same-session background/follow-up drains, and which scheduler layer should own that contract?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the fix changes core ordering and cancellation semantics for session state, background jobs, follow-up queues, and STOP behavior.

options.title: Adopt foreground-control priority
options.body: Make user and STOP/control turns structurally outrank background/follow-up work, with bounded abort/defer behavior for background tasks and regression tests for transcript ordering.

options.title: Add a narrow follow-up drain cap
options.body: Limit consecutive follow-up turns or elapsed drain time, yielding when fresh foreground work exists while leaving most current queue semantics intact.

options.title: Keep ordering and improve recovery
options.body: Treat the waits as acceptable serialized-session behavior and focus only on stuck diagnostics, operator warnings, and recovery timing.

recommendation.title: Adopt foreground-control priority
recommendation.body: Make user and STOP/control turns structurally outrank background/follow-up work, with bounded abort/defer behavior for background tasks and regression tests for transcript ordering.
